issue: The `optional` (off-Blueprint) flag is applied to only 7 of the 25 segment-reporting items, so identical content is in scope in one item and out of scope in the next. Learners who keep the default setting lose some segment practice but keep the rest, and the mocks contradict each other.
evidence: Flagged optional: far-sec-04 (operating-segment definition), -05 (revenue test), -06 (profit-test threshold), -07 (75% test), -09 (ASU 2023-07), -10 (asset test), far-x1-11 (revenue-test base; pulled from far-mock-1 per REVIEW.md P2-2). Unflagged items test the same facts the same way: far-sec-15/-25 (definition, CODM), -21 (revenue test), -16 and -27 (profit test), -17 and -28 (75% test), -33 (asset test), -18/-23/-31 (ASU 2023-07), -19/-32/-chk2 (major customer), -24/-34 (aggregation), and far-x1-27 (revenue test), which sits on far-mock-2 (content/far/exams/far-mock-2.json line 11). The lesson, flashcards fc5–fc8 and the segment part of TBS far-tbs-u2-analysis are also in scope. The FAR Area I group is titled 'Public company reporting topics (U.S. SEC reporting requirements, earnings per share and segment reporting)' (group name verified, per review/reference/blueprint-notes.md). far-standards.md §1c rates placement `conflict` because Becker lists 'disclosures for reportable segments' under BAR. Two web searches (results from superfastcpa.com, cpacredits.com, eduyush.com and accounting.uworld.com) place public company reporting in FAR Area I. Neither returned the task wording for segments.
source: AICPA 2026 FAR Blueprint, Area I group 'Public company reporting topics'; review/reference/blueprint-notes.md; review/reference/far-standards.md §1c; REVIEW.md 'Optional off-Blueprint material (P2-2)'
fix: Confirm the depth of segment coverage in the official 2026 FAR Blueprint PDF, then flag consistently. If the FAR group covers identifying reportable segments (most likely, given the group title), remove `optional` from far-sec-04, -05, -06, -07, -10 and far-x1-11. If only the disclosure detail is BAR, keep `optional` on far-sec-09 and add it to the other disclosure-only items (far-sec-18, -23, -31). Update REVIEW.md P2-2 to match.

issue: Five pure-recall items are labeled skill 'analysis' with difficulty 3. That is two skill levels too high, and it inflates the module's analysis share, which feeds the Blueprint skill-mix targets.
evidence: far-sec-30 ('An accelerated filer ... What is its Form 10-Q deadline?') is the same recall as far-sec-02, which is labeled remembering/1. far-sec-29 (a float of $800M gives a 10-K deadline) is the same task as far-sec-chk1 ($1.2B float) and far-sec-12, both labeled remembering, and the lesson objective calls deadline recall 'remembering'. far-sec-23 and -31 recall 'significant segment expenses', which far-sec-09 labels remembering/1. far-sec-25 recalls that the CODM is identified by function. None of the five asks the learner to examine interrelationships or draw inferences (the Blueprint's Analysis definition). cues.md shows analysis at 10 of 36 items; after relabeling, the module has 0 genuine analysis items.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions (Remembering & Understanding vs. Analysis)
fix: Relabel far-sec-23, -25, -29, -30 and -31 as skill 'remembering' with difficulty 1 (difficulty 2 is defensible for -29). If the module needs analysis items, write real multi-step ones (see the practice-design finding).

issue: The skill, difficulty and calc labels are each one level off, and inconsistent with matching items in the same module.
evidence: Labeled analysis/3 but single-step application: far-sec-27 (one 10% profit test), -28 (70% vs 75%; far-sec-07, the same task, is application/2/calc), -32 (12% vs 10%; chk2 and -19 are application/2), -33 (11% given vs 10%; far-sec-10, which needs a computation, is application/2), -34 (same fact as -24, which is application/2). Labeled application but pure recall: -18 (also difficulty 3), -22 (number of 8-K days), -24 (when aggregation is allowed), -26 (S-1 is the IPO form). far-sec-16 (profit-test threshold, with profits as the larger figure) is difficulty 3, but far-sec-06 (the harder variant, where losses are larger) is difficulty 2. far-sec-28 and -32 need a percentage computation but have calc=false, while far-sec-07 (6.3/9) has calc=true.
source: AICPA Blueprint skill definitions; src/content/schema.ts (skill, difficulty, calc)
fix: Set far-sec-27, -28, -32, -33, -34 to application with difficulty 1–2. Set far-sec-18, -22, -24, -26 to remembering with difficulty 1. Set far-sec-16 to difficulty 2. Set calc=true on far-sec-28 and -32, or calc=false on far-sec-07, so the three match.

issue: The stem does not say the company is a public entity. The major-customer disclosure in ASC 280-10-50-42 applies only to public entities. For a private company, the distractor 'Nothing' is defensible.
evidence: Stem: 'A customer provides $120,000 of a company's $1,000,000 revenue. What disclosure is required?' Revenue share is 120,000/1,000,000 = 12%, which is ≥ 10%. That triggers the ASC 280 disclosure only if ASC 280 applies (public entities, ASC 280-10-15-2). A nonpublic entity discloses a customer concentration only when the ASC 275-10-50-16/18 vulnerability criteria are met, so 'Nothing' can be the right answer. Compare far-sec-19 and far-sec-chk2, which both say 'public'.
fix: Reword the stem as: 'A public entity's single external customer provides $120,000 of its $1,000,000 consolidated revenue. Under ASC 280, what must it disclose?'

issue: Four places say the customer's identity is 'not' disclosed. They should say it 'need not' be disclosed: ASC 280 makes naming the customer optional, not prohibited.
evidence: Lesson body: 'disclose that fact, the amount, and the segment(s) — but **not** the customer's identity'. Lesson key takeaway: '(amount and segment, not the customer's name)'. fc8: '**not** the customer's name'. far-sec-chk2 (a) explanation: 'the customer is not named'. far-sec-32 explanation: 'but not the customer's name'. ASC 280-10-50-42 says the entity 'need not disclose the identity of a single external customer'. Many registrants do name such customers. far-sec-19 and chk2 (b) word it correctly ('need not' / 'not required').
fix: Reword all four places to 'the customer's identity need not be disclosed' (or 'is not required'), and drop the bold **not**.

issue: The two aggregation items state an incomplete rule. far-sec-24's key ('When economically similar') presents economic similarity alone as enough. far-sec-34's stem gives only three of the criteria, but the explanation says the criteria are met.
evidence: ASC 280-10-50-11 allows aggregation only if (1) it is consistent with the objective and basic principles of Topic 280, (2) the segments have similar economic characteristics, and (3) they are similar in each of five areas: products and services, production processes, type or class of customer, distribution methods, and regulatory environment. far-sec-24's key and its explanation 'Plus other similarity criteria' leave this to the learner. far-sec-34's stem covers economics, products and customers only.
fix: far-sec-24: change the key to 'When they have similar economic characteristics and are similar in each of the five qualitative areas (products, processes, customers, distribution, regulation)'. far-sec-34: add to the stem 'and are similar in production processes, distribution methods and regulatory environment', and list all five areas in the explanation.
